input.query: Identify the gravity context for the ground and flight observation entities from the supplied comparison passages. Propose at most two relations. Use hasGravityCondition, object_value normal-gravity or microgravity, context_scope group and quantifier IDENTIFIED. Quote the exact source words, preserving newlines. The names distinguish which group an entity represents; verify it from the documentary comparison rather than treating the investigation topic as a condition. Return a proposals array matching the required schema.

passages.text:
Material Ignition and Suppression Test
Carlos Fernandez-Pello, University of California, Berkeley
Objective

Understand the effect of space exploration atmospheres (SEA) on the piloted ignition under an
external radiant flux of a representative combustible material, as well as on its fire suppression
characteristics.
Status
― Three different diameters (0.25”, 0.375”, 0.5”) of black and clear PMMA rods were tested.
― Oxygen concentrations between 16% to 21% and flow velocity between 0.4 cm/sec to 4
cm/sec were tested. The total set of experiments yielded 54 unique flame spread rates.

There is a downward trend in flame
spread rate as sample diameter increases
for both the 1g and μg (microgravity)
tests. 1g tests have higher flame spread
rates than μg.

1g Black

Flame Spread Rate [cm/sec]

Flame spread rate as a function of
sample diameter for both 1g and μg
tests. 1g tests are in natural convection
at 21% oxygen environments. Values for
μg tests are averaged over flow velocity
and oxygen concentration.
